metric_catalog.label: Chill accumulation
metric_catalog.note: Profile-defined chill rule and six-month window; not chill portions.

metric_catalog.label: Winter freezing exposure
metric_catalog.note: Hourly temperature at or below the profile frost threshold during the chill window.

metric_catalog.label: Warm midwinter exposure
metric_catalog.note: T >21 C, 15 Nov to 15 Feb north, 15 May to 15 Aug south, inclusive UTC dates. Operational proxy, not measured chill negation.

metric_catalog.label: Lowest flowering temperature
metric_catalog.note: Minimum daily Tmin within the modelled flowering window.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering freeze exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmin <=-2.2 C under the legacy profile assumption; not an injury probability.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering rainfall
metric_catalog.note: Total rain within flowering; suspect rainfall is excluded by declining the metric.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering heavy rain
metric_catalog.note: Daily rain >=10 mm; operational exposure threshold.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Flowering mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Pollination-unfavourable weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmax <15 C OR rain >=1 mm. Operational cold/wet proxy, not literal bee inactivity; the cutoffs are not validated by UF IN1237.

metric_catalog.label: Cold-and-dry flowering weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmax <15 C AND rain <1 mm. Supervisor hypothesis comparison only, not an established pollination or loss index.

metric_catalog.label: Longest flowering dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Consecutive rain <1 mm, clipped to flowering. Not drought or soil water balance.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development heat exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmax >=32 C under the legacy assumption.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development severe heat exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmax >=35 C under the legacy assumption, not fruit temperature or measured injury.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-development disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Fruit-stage frost exposure
metric_catalog.note: Daily Tmin <=0 C. Generic exposure threshold, not stage-specific injury.

metric_catalog.label: Longest fruit-development dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Consecutive rain <1 mm, clipped to fruit development. Not drought or soil water balance.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest rainfall
metric_catalog.note: Total rain within the modelled harvest window.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest heavy rain
metric_catalog.note: Daily rain >=10 mm; operational exposure threshold.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest disease weather
metric_catalog.note: Tmean 15–28 C inclusive, RH >=85%, rain >=0.1 mm. Provisional daily proxy, not infection or the Blueberry Advisory System.

metric_catalog.label: Harvest mean VPD
metric_catalog.note: Calculated from daily mean temperature and RH, not hourly plant water stress.

metric_catalog.label: Longest production-window dry spell
metric_catalog.note: Rain <1 mm. New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain season start through harvest end.

metric_catalog.label: Production-window mean radiation
metric_catalog.note: New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain season start through harvest end.

metric_catalog.label: Production-window growing degree days
metric_catalog.note: Sum of max(Tmean minus profile base, 0). New primary uses budbreak through harvest end; legacy profiles retain the season-start window.

risks.note: Each winter uses its own stage dates. Ranked entries alone meet both reporting gates; equal frequencies share a competition rank and keep declared order. Missing windows are not safe years. Disease weather is one family with three complete stage windows. Frequent heavy rain is not a severity score; compare counts and totals. Dry spells, pollination weather and warm winter remain descriptive exposures.

changes: Northern calendar dates are reconstructed from the same 1 November anchor used for the offsets; the R summary used 1 October (-31 days).
Every site-year returns the same typed row with a status and per-metric issue reasons; incomplete years are never dropped or schema-split.
Chill, forcing and every stage metric require a complete, unique, ordered window; missing values are never compressed, zero-filled or counted as safe.
Suspect or out-of-range rainfall declines rain, dry-spell and disease-weather metrics for that window instead of contributing zero.
A non-positive chill requirement is refused (anchor_required); zero chill never silently anchors on the first winter date.
Headline risks require an event in at least half of at least 12 complete winters. Equal frequencies share a competition rank; no weighted total is produced.
The production system is reported three ways: from multi-year means (R behaviour), per-year distribution, and a two-thirds majority vote with transitional otherwise.
Winter-month features for the multi-feature rule come from our daily series (Jan-Mar north, Jul-Sep south of the winter year), not WorldClim monthly climatologies.
The stage_risks_v2 profile preserves the legacy chill and phenology constants. Crop exposures use each winter calendar, not the median calendar.
Disease weather combines complete flowering, fruit-development and harvest windows into one event family.
Warm midwinter hours use fixed hemisphere dates and remain available when the chill requirement fails.
limitations: Constants encode a UF-type low-chill southern highbush under open field + ground; they are provisional assumptions Paul set by judgement, not measured genotype parameters.
The calendar is a chill-triggered deciduous/semi-evergreen clock. Where the environment classifies as evergreen the production window is management-determined and this calendar does not apply.

NASA POWER grid cells (0.5 x 0.625 degrees) showed warm minimum-temperature bias against stations in the 2020 pilot; chill hours and freeze counts are therefore likely undercounted. No correction is applied.
UTC hours throughout. The original R requested local solar time; the difference affects window edges only.
Frequencies come from at most 15 winters; 95% Wilson intervals are shown and are wide. Do not over-read differences between sites.
Disease-favourable weather is a daily temperature/humidity/rain rule, not disease incidence. Longest dry spell is not a soil water balance.
Pollination-unfavourable days are an operational cold-or-wet proxy, not measured bee inactivity. Cold-and-dry days are a separate supervisor hypothesis comparison.
Fruit frost at or below 0 C is exposure, not a cultivar-specific injury threshold. Warm hours above 21 C are not measured chill negation.
The 50% frequency and 12-winter evidence gates are an explicit reporting policy, not biological loss thresholds. Dry spells, pollination weather and warm winter have no defined loss event.
No cultivar ranking, no soil scoring, no tunnel or pot effects, no forecast, no independent phenology validation yet.

hourly_source.note: Hourly temperature is one series per 0.5 x 0.625 degree source cell; every pin inside the cell receives the same chill and calendar.

assumptions: Open-field establishment in a prepared, well-drained acidic root zone with irrigation available.
Confirm nursery-stock dormancy, availability and planting timing with local Extension.
Remove first-season flowers or fruit; UGA also recommends removing most second-season flower buds on highbush plants.
limitations: Local soil workability, nursery availability, cultivar, plant condition and freeze protection still require confirmation.
This is a one-time establishment window, not annual replanting or a first-year harvest forecast.
No weather optimization, budbreak subtraction, or numerical tunnel/pot adjustment is applied.
Home-garden guidance covering several blueberry types. The range does not exclude suitable fall planting or establish commercial southern-highbush dates.
